181: #ifdef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
182:   /* Process wall time */
183: 
184:   clock_update_wall_time();
185: #endif
186: 
187:   /* Increment the system time (if in the link) */
188: 
189:   clock_timer();
190: 
191:   /* Check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
192:    * timeslice.
193:    */
194: 
195:   nxsched_process_scheduler();

202:   /* Call out to a user-provided function in order to perform board-specific,
203:    * custom timer operations.
204:    */
205:

40: /****************************************************************************
41:  * Name:  nxsched_process_delivered
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *    This function is used to process the tcb in g_delivertasks.
45:  * 1 We use direct locking instead of enter_critical_section
46:  * to save processing time
47:  * 2 If there is a higher priority task, we will still perform
48:  * the higher priority task
49:  * 3 If the schedule lock is on, the task will be placed in g_pendingtasks
50:  *
51:  * Input Parameters:
52:  *   cpu
53:  *
54:  * Returned Value:
55:  *   OK
56:  *
57:  * Assumptions:
58:  * - The caller must be in irq
59:  * - current cpu must not be locked
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: void nxsched_process_delivered(int cpu)
64: {
65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;
67: 
68:   DEBUGASSERT(up_interrupt_context());
69: 
70:   flags = enter_critical_section();
71:   priority = per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu);
72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;
73: 
74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&
75:       !nxsched_switch_running(cpu, priority == SWITCH_EQUAL))
76:     {
77:       /* Manage the (rare) case that task delivery to this CPU was not
78:        * successful. This can happen in two cases:
79:        * 1) The currently running task on this CPU just entered sched_lock
80:        * 2) This CPU just picked a higher priority task to execute
81:        *    before this SMP call was executed
82:        * To avoid schedule latency/priority inversion, just check once more
83:        * if there is another CPU eglible to run the delivered task, and
84:        * pass it forward.
85:        */
86: 
87:       FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
88:       if (tcb)
89:         {
90:           int target_cpu = tcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ?
91:             tcb->cpu : nxsched_select_cpu(tcb->affinity);
92:           if (target_cpu != cpu &&
93:               current_task(target_cpu)->sched_priority < tcb->sched_priority)
94:             {
95:               nxsched_deliver_task(cpu, target_cpu, priority);
96:             }
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:   leave_critical_section(flags);
101: }

740:  *     Will take spinlock each cpu first call.

742:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:

744:  *     Will only sched_lock once when first called.
745:  *

747:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s. not NULL.
748:  *
749:  * Returned Value:
750:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
751:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
752:  *
753:  ****************************************************************************/

755: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
756: static inline_function bool rspin_trylock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
757: {
758:   rspinlock_t new_val;
759:   rspinlock_t old_val;
760:   int         cpu = this_cpu() + 1;
761:   bool        ret = false;
762: 
763:   /* Already owned this lock. */
764: 
765:   old_val.val = atomic_read(&lock->val);
766: 
767:   if (old_val.owner == cpu)
768:     {
769:       lock->count += 1;
770:       ret = true;
771:     }
772:   else if (old_val.val == 0)
773:     {
774:       /* Try seize the ownership of the lock using CAS. */
775: 
776:       new_val.count = 1;
777:       new_val.owner = cpu;
778: 
779:       ret = atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->val,
780:                                    &old_val.val,
781:                                    new_val.val);
782: 
783:       /* Mark locked when the lock is successfully acquired. */
784: 
785:       if (ret)
786:         {
787:           spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
788:         }
789:     }
790: 
791:   return ret;
792: }

46:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
47:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
48:     {
49:       return false;
50:     }
51: 
52:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
53:   UP_DMB();
54:   return true;
55: }

57: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
58: {
59:   (void)dev;

61: }

64: {
65:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();

67:   (void)dev;

69:     {
70:       PANIC();
71:     }
72: 
73:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
74:   UP_DMB();
75:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
76:   UP_DSB();
77:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
78: }

84:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
85: };

91:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;

2:

5: `~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp`；可复现修改必须同时更新本目录及本文档。
6: 
7: ## 1. 当前覆盖文件

54: UART0 bridge 保持 `MB_UART0` 唯一初始化 owner。AP 输出 LOG 模式保留 `ap0:`
55: 前缀、50 ms 半行刷新和有限重试；RAW 模式不改写字节。PC 到 AP 输入使用
56: 1024 B 有界 ring 和部分写 worker，所有物理 UART0 输出仍经 shell queue 串行化。
57: 
58: `ram_regions.csv`采用原厂 `lvgl/img_decode`、`lvgl/freetype_font` 的 16 MiB
59: 七区域布局：
60: 
61: ```text
62: 0x60000000..0x60700000  四个媒体 slab，共 7 MiB
63: 0x60700000..0x60720000  CP PSRAM heap，128 KiB
64: 0x60720000..0x60a00000  AP PSRAM heap，2.875 MiB
65: 0x60a00000..0x61000000  AP PSRAM section，6 MiB
66: ```

191: 
192: 修改以下任一输入后，不得直接做 SMP 增量构建：
193: 
194: - `ram_regions.csv`
195: - AP/CP `config`
196: - Kconfig 默认值
197: - 分区生成脚本

303: ## 5. OpenVela PSRAM 接入状态
304: 
305: OpenVela AP侧已经完成以下代码和离线构建基线：
306: 
307: - 精确16 MiB、RW/XN/non-cacheable MPU映射。
308: - `0x60720000..0x609fffff`独立AP PSRAM heap。
309: - USER/AUDIO/ENCODE/DISPLAY四个独立媒体pool。
310: - 明确排除`0x60700000..0x6071ffff` CP heap的地址检查。
311: - AP owner区域保存/恢复型alias probe，包含4/8/12 MiB测试点。
312: - `0x60a00000..0x60ffffff`静态section链接保留；reset copy/clear未实现前强制0 B。
313: 
314: 本覆盖中的CP `0x7`协议要求request `param3=PM_PSRAM_PROTO_V1`；response `param1`回显
315: ON/OFF state、`param2`返回真实PSRAM driver结果、`param3`回显version。CP BOOT与
316: OpenVela使用独立owner，初始化失败不置owner bit。`0xc`已提供frequency/divider、
317: speed、voltage、CPU power/reset和PSRAM owner只读诊断；device ID和actual capacity
318: 仍未暴露，因此alias probe和整颗器件实板测试仍是容量门禁。AP board必须同步发送
319: V1 version并检查真实ret/version后才能联调；本CP侧任务未修改AP board代码。
320: 
321: PWC ready 使用两阶段契约：AP 的既有 `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD=0x5` 仅解除 CP boot
322: worker 等待，不发布最终 PWC/bridge ready。新增 `PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD=0x11` 由 mailbox
323: ISR 排入 low-power worker；`param1=1` 表示 AP 已完成 PSRAM/SMP commit，CP 只有在
324: boot stage 5、CPU1/CPU2 power、CPU2 hold、480 MHz clock 和 OpenVela PSRAM owner
325: 全部通过 readback 后才进入 stage 6 并发布 PWC ready。`param1=0` 时 `param2` 必须是
326: 真实负 errno，CP 执行 best-effort 完整 rollback。正常 recovery 的 INIT/拒绝会取消
327: shutdown 并恢复 boot vote；只有 FINISH 才进入 shutdown。CP 不实现 runtime DVFS/P1，
328: 也不在 recovery INIT 路径直接停止 CPU2。
329: 
330: 实板首次联调发现 AP 在 `arm_serialinit()` 的 scheduler-lock 上下文中等待新建 mailbox
331: worker，导致 worker 无法运行、物理 mailbox 未启动便进入 SMP，最终 CP 在 stage 4
332: 收不到 `0x5`。当前 AP 已拆分初始化：early serial 阶段只初始化逻辑状态、物理 MBOX
333: IRQ 和 console，`AppBringUp` 再启动 mailbox/MB-UART worker 并验证 CPU0 affinity。
334: `0x5` 也已移到 PWC callback 注册后、heartbeat/PWC worker 启动前。CP stage-4 等待
335: 窗口由3秒放宽为10秒，失败时保留错误和 rollback 现场，不再由 `cp_main` 断言触发
336: 整芯片循环复位；最终 `0x11` commit 条件不变。
337: 
338: 第二次实板联调仍停在 stage 4，且 CP 未收到 AP IPC power-up。AP early serial 中
339: `bk7258_mb_uart_init()` 的初始化 `printf()` 发生在 idle stdio 建立前，现已移除。
340: 同时在 AP_SPINLOCK 尾部 `0x2800ffe0..0x2800ffff` 加入不依赖 mailbox/console 的启动
341: 轨迹；CP timeout 会打印 `AP trace=<magic> primary=<stage> secondary=<stage>` 和5个
342: detail word。magic 应为 `0x41505452`。primary 1..4 表示 CPU1入口至 `nx_start`，
343: 10..14 表示 early serial，20..24 表示 CPU2启动/IPI，30..34 表示 late bring-up至
344: `0x5` transport ACK；secondary 1..5 表示 CPU2入口、private、NVIC、mailbox和idle。
345: 
346: 共享轨迹首次返回 `primary=2, secondary=0`，证明 CPU1 已进入 `bk7258_start()`，但
347: 未完成主核 private 初始化。根因是启动代码在清零 BSS 前调用 `modifyreg32()` 开启
348: CPACR，而 NuttX `modifyreg32()` 使用 BSS 中的 spinlock；AP-only reset 后保留 SRAM
349: 可令该锁保持占用，CPU1 永久自旋。当前已改为与 Armino `SystemInitCpu0()` 一致的
350: 无锁 CPACR 直接读改写。`__start` 同时清零全部 detail word；primary 5/6/7/8/9
351: 分别表示 CPACR、data copy、BSS clear、runtime vector copy 和 atomic gate 初始化完成。
352: 
353: 下一轮轨迹返回 `primary=22, secondary=5`，证明 CPU1 已释放 CPU2 reset，CPU2 已完成
354: private/NVIC/mailbox 初始化并进入 secondary idle，但主核没有观察到 online。原实现
355: 在 online 发布前开启 CPU2 全局中断，且 online/boot-test flag 全部使用同一个 libc
356: atomic hwspinlock；CPU1 以480 MHz紧密轮询该非公平锁，可令 CPU2 的一次 store 永久
357: 饥饿，原厂 Armino secondary scheduler handoff 也不会在发布 ready 前开启中断。当前
358: bootstrap 已改为专用 raw Mailbox `BOOT_NOTIFY/BOOT_PING` 和 volatile shared flag加
359: barrier，不再依赖通用 atomic gate；CPU2 顺序固定为interrupt stack、online、notify、
360: 最后开中断。secondary 6/7/8/9分别表示这四个阶段。正常 scheduler/call IPI 仍使用
361: 原 atomic pending 状态机；500 ms诊断轮询中的无界 `wfe` 也已移除。
362: 
363: 再下一轮轨迹推进到 `primary=22, secondary=9`，证明 CPU2 已完成 stack、notify 和
364: 全局中断开启，而 CPU1仍未完成启动握手。`primary=22` 还可能表示 CPU1在第一次
365: 读取系统 tick或等待 CPU1 Mailbox IRQ 时停住；该阶段不能要求 arch timer 已可靠
366: 递增，也不应依赖启动期 IRQ 调度或跨核共享 ready flag。当前握手因此改为完全由
367: 硬件 FIFO证明：CPU2发送 `BOOT_NOTIFY`，CPU1屏蔽本核中断并主动 drain channel 1，
368: 收到 notify 后向 CPU2发送 `BOOT_PING`，CPU2的 channel 2 IRQ回 `BOOT_ACK`，CPU1
369: 轮询收到 ACK 后才返回 `up_cpu_start()`。CPU1只更新自己的本地状态，不再读取
370: CPU2写入的 online flag；DWT cycle counter和纯迭代上限共同保证 AP先于 CP的10秒
371: 门限留下诊断。secondary stage 10表示 CPU2已收到 ping并发出 ACK。
372: 
373: 该版本实板轨迹为 `primary=24, secondary=10`，确认双向 hardware FIFO handshake 已
374: 完整成功，停点已移动到 CPU1恢复本核中断或紧随其后的 NuttX SMP启动收尾。CPU1
375: 主动 drain channel 1时硬件仍可能保留 Mailbox NVIC pending；当前在恢复中断前显式
376: 清除该 pending，并把窗口继续拆分：primary 25表示准备恢复中断，26表示首个 IRQ已
377: 进入（detail[2]保存 IRQ号，15是 SysTick、79是 Mailbox），27表示恢复中断调用已
378: 返回，28表示 `up_cpu_start()` 即将成功返回，30仍表示 board late bring-up入口。
379: 
380: 细分后的实板轨迹为 `primary=26, secondary=10, detail[2]=0x0f`，精确确认 CPU1
381: 永久停在恢复中断后的首个 SysTick。首 tick 的 scheduler/atomic路径会立即使用 libc
382: 全局 atomic gate，而原 gate以 SRAM `LDAEX/STREX`实现。BK7258原厂 spinlock源码
383: 明确说明芯片只有两个 SRAM exclusive monitor，并对三个活跃核心参与 exclusive
384: access的配置直接编译报错；当前 CP、AP CPU1和AP CPU2三核同时运行，AP exclusive
385: 序列可能永久失败。当前 AP-only atomic gate已改为两个AP逻辑核之间的 Peterson锁，
386: 只使用位于 inner-shareable non-cacheable AP_SPINLOCK区的普通对齐 word store和
387: barrier，不再占用 exclusive monitor。NuttX上层 atomic/hwspinlock API保持不变，
388: `.bk_spinlock`由4字节增至16字节。
389: 
390: Peterson gate版本实板仍返回相同的 `primary=26, detail[2]=0x0f`，因此 exclusive
391: monitor是必须消除的独立三核风险，但不是当前首 tick停点的充分解释。继续对照原厂
392: FreeRTOS SMP发现其固定 `configTICK_CORE=CPU0`，tick owner直接推进内核 tick；当前
393: NuttX配置却启用了 `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH`，将SysTick包装为通用 timer lower-half，首 tick
394: 的 watchdog时间查询又通过 `clock_systime_ticks()`回读正在执行的同一 SysTick
395: lower-half。当前已关闭 `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH`，改为 logical CPU0专属的直接 SysTick ISR，
396: CPU2继续保持私有 SysTick关闭；生成配置和最终 map已确认不再包含 `timer_callback`、
397: `up_timer_gettick`或`systick_initialize`，系统时间恢复为 `g_system_ticks`。首 tick新增
398: detail[3]诊断：0表示尚未进入BK7258 timer ISR，1表示已进入并正在执行
399: `nxsched_process_timer()`，2表示timer核心处理已返回。

435: ## 7. UART0 Mailbox V2 使用和边界
436: 
437: CP 启动后默认 owner 为 `CP_CLI`。只有 MB_UART0 STATE 成功 ACK、IPC power-up 和
438: PWC boot-ready 三个条件同时成立，且`bk_mb_uart_write_ready()`非零时，
439: `ap_console open`才允许进入。heartbeat timeout、AP reset/power-off 和 Mailbox
440: reset/timeout都会清除门禁并请求回退到CP CLI。使用方式：
441: 
442: ```text
443: ap_console status
444: ap_console open
445: <RAW AP NSH interaction>
446: <press Ctrl-], release it, then press .>
447: ap_console status
448: ```
449: 
450: `open`在当前 CP CLI 响应经 UART TX-complete 后生效，并清 CP parser 和 UART RX；
451: RAW 模式不添加前缀。退出时按下`Ctrl-]`、松开，再按`.`；该转义不依赖行首状态。
452: 链路 reset/timeout/down 时自动清理
453: 未发送输入并回到 `CP_CLI`。`status`输出 owner/link/mode、bridge ring、MB_UART 状态、
454: active channel/sequence/command 和 drop/partial/overflow/reset/timeout 统计。

102:  *
103:  * Description:
104:  *   Check if the currently executing task has exceeded its time slice.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   tcb - The TCB of the currently executing task
108:  *   ticks - The number of ticks that have elapsed on the interval timer.
109:  *   noswitches - True: Can't do context switches now.
110:  *
111:  * Returned Value:
112:  *   The number if ticks remaining until the next time slice expires.
113:  *   CLOCK_MAX is returned if there is no time slicing (i.e., the task at
114:  *   the head of the ready-to-run list does not support round robin
115:  *   scheduling).
116:  *
117:  *   The value one may returned under certain circumstances that probably
118:  *   can't happen.  The value one is the minimal timer setup and it means
119:  *   that a context switch is needed now, but cannot be performed because
120:  *   noswitches == true.
121:  *
122:  * Assumptions:
123:  *   - Interrupts are disabled
124:  *   - The task associated with TCB uses the round robin scheduling
125:  *     policy

129: clock_t nxsched_process_roundrobin(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, clock_t ticks,
130:                                    bool noswitches)
131: {
132:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;  /* Pointer to the next ready-to-run TCB */
133:   clock_t ret;
134:   int decr;
135: 
136:   /* How much can we decrement the timeslice delay?  If 'ticks' is greater
137:    * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138:    *
139:    * 'ticks' should not be greater than the remaining timeslice.  But that
140:    * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been
141:    * disabled or the noswitches flag is set.  This might cause jitter of a
142:    * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.
143:    */
144: 
145:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL);
146:   decr = MIN(tcb->timeslice, ticks);
147: 
148:   /* Decrement the timeslice counter */
149: 
150:   tcb->timeslice -= decr;
151: 
152:   /* Did decrementing the timeslice counter cause the timeslice to expire? */
153: 
154:   ret = tcb->timeslice;
155:   if (tcb->timeslice <= 0 && !nxsched_islocked_tcb(tcb))
156:     {
157:       /* We will also suppress context switches if we were called via one
158:        * of the unusual cases handled by nxsched_reassess_timer().  In that
159:        * case, we will return a value of one so that the timer will expire
160:        * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161:        * timer expiration context.
162:        *
163:        * This is kind of kludge, but I am not to concerned because I hope
164:        * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165:        * rare corner-cases.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (noswitches)
169:         {
170:           ret = 0;
171:         }
172:       else
173:         {
174:           /* Reset the timeslice. */
175: 
176:           tcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
177:           ret = tcb->timeslice;
178: 
179:           /* We know we are at the head of the ready to run prioritized
180:            * list.  We must be the highest priority task eligible for
181:            * execution.  Check the next task in the ready to run list.  If
182:            * it is the same priority, then we need to relinquish the CPU and
183:            * give that task a shot.
184:            */

186: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
187:           ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
188: #else
189:           ptcb = tcb->flink;
190: #endif
191:           if (ptcb &&
192:               ptcb->sched_priority >= tcb->sched_priority)
193:             {
194:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
195: 
196:               /* Just resetting the task priority to its current value.
197:                * This will cause the task to be rescheduled behind any
198:                * other tasks at the same priority.
199:                */
200: 
201: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
202:               DEBUGASSERT(tcb->task_state == TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING);
203:               if (tcb->cpu != this_cpu())
204:                 {
205:                   nxsched_smp_call_init(&g_call_data,
206:                                         nxsched_roundrobin_handler,
207:                                         (FAR void *)(uintptr_t)tcb->pid);
208:                   nxsched_smp_call_single_async(tcb->cpu, &g_call_data);
209:                 }
210:               else if (nxsched_switch_running(tcb->cpu, true))
211: #else
212:               if (nxsched_reprioritize_rtr(tcb, tcb->sched_priority))
213: #endif
214:                 {
215:                   nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
216:                 }

221:     {
222:       ret = CLOCK_MAX;
223:     }

79:     (
80:       "msr psp, r0\n"
81: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
82:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
83: #endif
84:       "mrs r1, control\n"
85:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
86:       "msr control, r1\n"

101:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);

103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);

122:       "movs r0, #1\n"
123:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
124:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
125:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
126:       "msr msplim, r0\n"

131: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
132: {
133:   irqstate_t flags;
134:   uint32_t started;
135:   uint32_t polls = 0;
136:   uint32_t control;
137:   uint32_t status;
138:   bool ping_sent = false;
139: 
140:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
141: 
142:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
143:     {
144:       return -EINVAL;
145:     }
146: 
147:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
148:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
149:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
150:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
151:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
152:     {
153:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
154:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
155:       PANIC();
156:     }
157: 
158:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
159:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
160:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
161:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
162:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
163:     {
164:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
165:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
166:       PANIC();
167:     }
168: 
169:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
170:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
171:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
172: 
173:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
174:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
175:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
176:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
177:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
178:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
179:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
180:   UP_DMB();
181:   UP_DSB();
182: 
183:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
184:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
185:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
186:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
187:   flags = up_irq_save();
188:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
189:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
190:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
191:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
192: 
193:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
194:     {
195:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
196:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
197:         {
198:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
199:             {
200:               break;
201:             }
202: 
203:           ping_sent = true;
204:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
205:         }
206: 
207:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
208:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
209:         {
210:           break;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
215:     {
216:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
217:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
218:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
219:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
220:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
221:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
222:       up_irq_restore(flags);
223:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
224:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
225:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
226:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
227:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
228:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
229:       PANIC();
230:     }
231: 
232:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
233:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
234:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
235:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
236:   UP_DSB();
237:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
238:   up_irq_restore(flags);
239:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
240:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
241:   return OK;
242: }

# 1. Vendor/original FreeRTOS startup

## 1.1 Primary CPU starts the scheduler and releases the secondary AP core

The vendor FreeRTOS SMP scheduler starts on logical CPU0. `xPortStartScheduler()`:

1. Validates that it is running on CPU0.
2. Sets `ucPrimaryCoreNum = configTICK_CORE`.
3. Initializes the cross-core mailbox.
4. Calls `multicore_launch_core1()`.
5. Delays with a fixed busy loop.
6. Starts the scheduler on the primary core.

Citations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1202-1225`
- The same implementation is present in the preserved original tree:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1202-1225`

The relevant vendor code is:

```c
ucPrimaryCoreNum = configTICK_CORE;
configASSERT(portGET_CORE_ID() == 0);
bk_mailbox_cc_init();
multicore_launch_core1(prvDisableInterruptsAndPortStartSchedulerOnCore);
for (volatile uint32_t i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
xPortStartSchedulerOnCore();
```

The fixed delay is explicitly described as avoiding the primary scheduler starting before the other core has completed enough startup, rather than as a handshake:

```c
for(volatile uint32_t i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
```

There is no vendor equivalent of the current OpenVela hardware FIFO `BOOT_NOTIFY → BOOT_PING → BOOT_ACK` transaction.

## 1.4 Vendor secondary interrupt initialization is broad and early

Vendor `secondary_core_interrupt_init()` initializes the secondary NVIC and then enables every interrupt source listed in the ICU table:

The vendor scheduler core path is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:962-1003`

cpsie i
cpsie f
dsb
isb
svc %0

The first context is then selected through the SVC handler:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:789-811`

2. Global `cpsie i`

The secondary physical CPU is held and released through explicit CPU2 control bits:

## 3.2 Current secondary entry starts with interrupts disabled

Current secondary entry is a naked function:

This assigns logical NuttX CPU1 by writing `1` to the CPU-ID location, establishes the bootstrap stack limit, and branches directly into C startup while global interrupts are still disabled.

The current secondary idle handoff is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:59-71`

bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);

...

```c

...

```

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:116-129`

# 3. Meaning of `detail3=2`

The SysTick ISR is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:33-51`

```c
static int bk7258_timerisr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
{
  if (primary_stage() == 26)
    detail(3, 1);

  nxsched_process_timer();

  if (primary_stage() == 26)
    detail(3, 2);

  return OK;
}
```

The current ELF disassembly at `0x021506a8` is:

```asm
0x021506b4: movs r3, #1
0x021506b6: str.w r3, [trace, #0xff8]  ; detail3 = 1
...
0x021506be: bl nxsched_process_timer
...
0x021506ca: movs r3, #2
0x021506cc: str.w r3, [trace, #0xff8]  ; detail3 = 2
...
0x021506d4: movs r0, #0
0x021506d6: pop {r4, pc}
```

Thus:

```text
detail3 = 2
```

means that the call to `nxsched_process_timer()` has returned all the way back to `bk7258_timerisr()`, and the ISR has written the post-return probe.

This is stronger than merely proving that `clock_timer()` completed. It also means the subsequent timer-processing portions completed, including:

- scheduler tick policy processing;
- the SMP scheduler loop;
- watchdog processing via `wd_timer()`;
- the return from the timer processing path.

The compiler has tail-called `wd_timer()` from `nxsched_process_timer()`, but the original caller’s link register is restored before the branch. Consequently, `detail3=2` is written only after the watchdog call has also returned.

The current disassembly of `nxsched_process_timer()` is at `0x021668dc`. It includes:

- `clock_timer()` at `0x021668e0`;
- scheduler/round-robin logic;
- `clock_systime_ticks()`;
- tail-call to `wd_timer()`.

Therefore the earlier failure hypothesis “stuck inside the first `clock_timer()` atomic operation” does not describe a capture with `detail3=2`. The stop is later.

# 4. IRQ vector and exception-entry structure

The runtime vector table is defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_vectors.c:45-52`

```c
const vector_t _vectors[NR_IRQS] =
{
  [0]       = __idle_stack_top,
  [1]       = __start,
  [2 ... 14] = exception_common,
  [15 ...]   = exception_direct,
};
```

This is decisive:

- PendSV is IRQ 14 and uses `exception_common`.
- SysTick is IRQ 15 and uses `exception_direct`.

## SysTick path

```text
SysTick exception entry
  -> exception_direct
      -> arm_ack_irq(15)
      -> irq_dispatch(15, NULL)
          -> bk7258_timerisr
              -> nxsched_process_timer
              -> detail3 = 2
      -> compare running task state
      -> possibly pend PendSV
      -> return with EXC_RETURN
  -> normal thread execution resumes
      -> stage 27 can execute
```

`exception_direct()` is at `0x02159074`:

```asm
push {r3,r4,r5,lr}
mrs  r4, IPSR
...
mov  r0, r4
bl   arm_ack_irq
...
mov  r0, r4
movs r1, #0
bl   irq_dispatch
...
compare g_running_tasks[cpu] with g_assignedtasks[cpu]
...
if different:
    up_trigger_irq(PendSV, 0)
...
pop {..., lr}
bx   lr
```

The SysTick handler does not call `arm_doirq()` and does not execute the full software context-save path.

## PendSV path

PendSV vector 14 enters `exception_common`, then:

```text
exception_common
  -> save hardware/software/FPU context
  -> arm_doirq(14, regs)
      -> tcb->xcp.regs = regs
      -> nxsched_suspend_scheduler()
      -> board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ)
      -> arm_ack_irq(14)
      -> PendSV-specific scheduler/signal logic
      -> possibly task selection
      -> nxsched_resume_scheduler()
      -> board_autoled_off(LED_INIRQ)
      -> tcb->xcp.regs = NULL
      -> return selected regs
  -> restore registers, BASEPRI, CONTROL, PSP/MSP, PSPLIM
  -> bx EXC_RETURN
```

`exception_common` is at `0x02159472`; `arm_doirq` is at `0x021590d0`.

# 6. `up_irq_save()` and `up_irq_restore()`

For ARMv8-M with BASEPRI, the definitions are:

In the current ELF, `up_cpu_start()` saves the old BASEPRI before releasing CPU2:

It later restores it:

The relevant consequences are:

2. `up_irq_restore(flags)` lowers BASEPRI, normally back to zero.
3. SysTick is then accepted.
4. Stage 27 is after the restore instruction.
5. Any interrupt accepted in that window can delay stage 27.
6. `up_irq_restore()` itself is not a locking function and does not call the scheduler.
7. It does not restore PRIMASK; it only restores BASEPRI in this ARMv8-M build.

The primary startup code previously called `up_irq_enable()` during IRQ initialization:

# 8. PendSV and context-switch behavior after the ISR

After `irq_dispatch()` returns, `exception_direct()` compares:

- `g_running_tasks[cpu]`
- `g_assignedtasks[cpu]`

The ELF locations are:

```text
g_running_tasks:  0x280283dc
g_assignedtasks: 0x280283e8
```

This is the post-direct-IRQ scheduling handoff:

```c
if (g_running_task != this_task())
  {
    up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0);
  }
```

The ARMv8-M implementation uses equivalent compiled logic in `exception_direct()`.

If the pointers differ:

1. `up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0)` writes the PendSV pending bit.
2. The SysTick handler returns from `exception_direct()`.
3. The Cortex-M exception controller may tail-chain directly into PendSV instead of returning to thread mode.
4. PendSV enters `exception_common`.
5. `arm_doirq()` performs the scheduler/context-switch processing.
6. Only after PendSV completes can the interrupted `up_cpu_start()` code execute stage 27.

Thus stage 27 does not prove merely that the SysTick ISR returned. It proves that the whole sequence before the stage-27 instruction returned to the CPU0 thread, including any immediately required PendSV processing.

A task mismatch is not expected merely because `nxsched_process_timer()` ran. On the first tick, the system is still inside `nx_smp_start()` in `nx_start()`, before normal `nx_bringup()`:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:805-826`

At that point the main active tasks should still be the idle tasks. This makes an unexpected `g_running_tasks`/`g_assignedtasks` mismatch less likely, but it remains the key branch to verify with a debugger or additional trace.

# 9. Stack limit, interrupt stack, and MPU

## Interrupt-stack layout

The linker map gives:

```text
__intstacks_start = 0x2802ac80
__intstacks_end   = 0x2802bc80
```

The build asserts two 2048-byte stacks:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/ld.script.tmp:153-156`

CPU0 interrupt stack:

```text
0x2802ac80 .. 0x2802b480
```

CPU1 interrupt stack:

```text
0x2802b480 .. 0x2802bc80
```

The BK-specific `up_get_intstackbase()` is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:31-35`

```c
return g_bk7258_intstacks + cpu * INTSTACK_SIZE;
```

## CPU0 startup stack setup

`__start()` initially sets:

```asm
msr msplim, __idle_stack_base
```

Then `bk7258_start()` calls `arm_initialize_stack()` after CPU-private setup.

`arm_initialize_stack()` sets:

- MSP to the current CPU’s interrupt-stack top;
- MSPLIM to the current CPU’s interrupt-stack base;
- PSP appropriately;
- PSPLIM appropriately when hardware stack checking is enabled.

For CPU0, the initial runtime interrupt stack is therefore separate from the CPU0 idle thread stack.

## SysTick versus common exception stack handling

For SysTick through `exception_direct`:

- the processor performs normal hardware exception stacking;
- handler mode uses MSP;
- the direct C handler pushes `{r4, lr}`;
- there is no software save of FPU/nonvolatile registers;
- there is no software manipulation of MSPLIM/PSPLIM;
- there is no `tcb->xcp.regs`.

For PendSV through `exception_common`:

- the assembly explicitly disables the active stack limit while reserving software exception context;
- it saves the previous stack-limit value in the context;
- it restores MSP/PSP and MSPLIM/PSPLIM from the selected context;
- it restores BASEPRI and CONTROL;
- it exits via `bx lr` using EXC_RETURN.

The common epilogue is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_exception.S:298-337`

The current ELF disassembly is at `0x02159472`.

## MPU

The MPU is initialized before `nx_start()` in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:107-149`

The relevant regions include:

- AP flash, read-only;
- AP RAM, read/write, inner-shareable, non-cacheable;
- AP spinlock area `0x28000000`;
- CP RAM;
- mailbox buffers;
- optional PSRAM;
- device region at `0x40000000`.

The spinlock and boottrace regions are explicitly covered by the AP spinlock MPU region:

```text
BK7258_AP_SPINLOCK_BASE = 0x28000000
BK7258_AP_SPINLOCK_SIZE = 0x00010000
```

There is no obvious MPU mapping defect in the direct SysTick path. A stack-limit or MPU fault remains possible during automatic exception unstacking or a later PendSV restore, but `detail3=2` proves that the C ISR body itself completed.

## Candidate 1: Atomic-gate spin in the immediate post-ISR PendSV trigger

This is the strongest concrete post-`detail3=2` software candidate, conditional on a task mismatch.

The post-dispatch code can call:

```text
exception_direct
  -> up_trigger_irq(PendSV)
  -> modifyreg32(NVIC_INTCTRL, ...)
  -> atomic_lock()
```

`modifyreg32()` uses a global spinlock:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/common/arm_modifyreg.c:94-104`

The ELF implementation at `0x02159370` uses:

```text
atomic_fetch_add_4()
atomic_load_4()
wait until owner/turn condition
```

`atomic_lock()` is at `0x0215d138` and loops until the BK7258 hwspinlock operation succeeds.

The current gate is the AP-only Peterson implementation:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c`

The current build no longer uses the old three-core SRAM-exclusive implementation, but CPU0 and CPU1 can still contend for this software gate. A failed `atomic_lock()` is an unbounded loop.

Why it fits:

- `detail3=2` proves all timer-body atomics completed.
- The next potentially blocking code is the post-dispatch mismatch path.
- Stage 27 is not written until after `exception_direct` returns.
- `up_trigger_irq()` calls `modifyreg32()`, which can spin indefinitely.
- The gate has diagnostic `detail4` values specifically intended to identify this path.

What would strengthen this diagnosis:

- `detail4` ending in one of the Peterson-gate markers while primary remains 26;
- debugger PC in `atomic_lock()`, `bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock()`, or `modifyreg32()`;
- `g_running_tasks[0] != g_assignedtasks[0]`.

Important qualification: if the two task pointers are equal, this path is not entered.

This is closely related to Candidate 1 but includes the full exception/context-switch path.

If `exception_direct()` observes a task mismatch, it pends PendSV. The processor may tail-chain from SysTick directly into PendSV. Stage 27 cannot execute until PendSV completes.

Potential blocking points include:

1. `board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ)`;
2. `arm_doirq()` scheduler suspension/resumption;
3. signal handling;
4. atomic/spinlock operations in scheduler code;
5. `board_autoled_off(LED_INIRQ)`;
6. common exception context restore;
7. PSP/MSP/PSPLIM restoration;
8. automatic exception return.

Evidence:

- `exception_direct()` at `0x02159074` explicitly pends PendSV on a task mismatch.
- PendSV vector 14 uses `exception_common`.
- `arm_doirq()` stores `tcb->xcp.regs`, performs scheduler operations, and clears it on exit.
- `arm_doirq()` invokes LED hooks.
- The build has SMP, RR scheduling, signals, FPU, MPU, and hardware stack checking.

The LED subpath is particularly concrete:

```text
board_autoled_on()

      -> modifyreg32()

However, because SysTick itself uses `exception_direct`, the LED hooks are not involved until a PendSV or another common exception is entered.

## Candidate 3: Immediate interrupt re-entry/starvation after `up_irq_restore()`

Stage 27 is after:

```asm
msr BASEPRI, r8
```

and there is no barrier before the stage-27 call.

Once BASEPRI is restored, any pending or newly arriving interrupt can be accepted before the trace write. Possibilities include:

- another SysTick;
- a mailbox IRQ;
- an IRQ caused by the CPU2 handshake or mailbox activity;
- PendSV if it was pended by `exception_direct()`.

This can delay stage 27 or, in an interrupt-storm situation, starve the thread indefinitely.

Evidence:

- Stage 25 is deliberately written before interrupt restoration.
- The mailbox pending bit is explicitly cleared before stage 25:
  `bk7258_cpustart.c:234-238`.
- The first interrupt is nevertheless SysTick, not mailbox.
- `up_irq_restore()` is exactly the operation immediately preceding stage 27.
- The SysTick is enabled at `bk7258_timerisr.c:70-81`.

This is a plausible explanation for a trace that remains at primary 26 even though `detail3=2`, but a normal 1 kHz SysTick should not repeatedly preempt the few instructions needed to reach stage 27. It becomes more credible if the SysTick is re-pending immediately because of a hardware/reload/configuration issue or if another IRQ continuously reasserts.

## Candidate 4: Fault during automatic SysTick exception unstacking

`detail3=2` is written before `exception_direct()` returns. The automatic hardware exception return has not yet happened.

The direct handler returns through:

```asm
pop {r3,r4,r5,lr}
bx  lr
```

where `lr` is the EXC_RETURN value.

A MemManage, BusFault, UsageFault, SecureFault, or HardFault during exception unstacking would leave primary at 26 and detail3 at 2.

Possible causes would include:

- corrupted hardware-stacked frame;
- invalid return EXC_RETURN;
- MSP/PSP corruption;
- stack-limit violation;
- corrupted xPSR/PC;
- memory access failure while unstacking.

Why it is lower ranked:

- `exception_direct()` saves and restores LR in a simple, visible sequence.
- SysTick does not manipulate `tcb->xcp.regs`, PSP, PSPLIM, or the software context frame.
- The interrupt stacks are aligned and linker-checked.
- The current trace proves the ISR’s C body returned normally.

This remains a concrete hardware-level possibility, especially if a fault handler or reset path is not externally visible in the boottrace area.

This is distinct from direct SysTick unstacking.

If PendSV is tail-chained, `exception_common` restores:

MSP or PSP

- `CONFIG_ARM_MPU=y`.
- The common assembly explicitly restores PSPLIM/MSPLIM.

## Candidate 6: Incorrect task-pointer state causes an unexpected PendSV

The post-SysTick direct path compares:

```text

g_assignedtasks[0]
```

These are different concepts:

- `g_running_tasks[]` is the interrupt-context reference.
- `g_assignedtasks[]` is the task assigned to each CPU.

The arrays are initialized during idle-task initialization:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:340-379`

## Candidate 7: Mailbox/CP interaction

The CP does not directly execute the AP’s exception epilogue. The first observed IRQ is SysTick, not the mailbox IRQ, and the mailbox pending bit was explicitly cleared before interrupts were restored.

Therefore CP activity is not the primary direct explanation for `detail3=2` followed by no stage 27.

- contending with AP traffic at the interconnect;
- causing an AP mailbox handler to enter an atomic gate;
- generating continuous mailbox work that postpones AP progress.

The current AP atomic gate is explicitly intended to be AP-only, so CP should not own it directly. The CP is more likely an indirect interrupt/traffic source than the immediate lock owner.

**结论**

这次日志已经把卡点从“首个 SysTick 内部”推进到：

```text
SysTick IRQ 进入
  -> nxsched_process_timer()
  -> atomic/Peterson gate 完整释放
  -> nxsched_process_timer() 返回
  -> detail3=2
  -> 卡在 exception_direct() 后半段、PendSV/tail-chain 或异常返回之前
```

CP 超时不是电源、时钟、PSRAM 或 CPU2 启动失败。AP 已经完成物理 CPU2 的启动握手，但还没有走到 OpenVela 向 CP 发送 `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD=0x5` 的阶段。

---

**启动时序**

从日志看，时序如下：

```text
11:08:20.196  AP mailbox UART bridge 初始化
11:08:20.210  PSRAM 初始化成功
11:08:20.319  Wi-Fi 初始化成功
11:08:28.314  CP 等待 AP 启动期间第 4 次 IPC retry
11:08:30.314  CP 等待 CPU1/AP 启动超时
11:08:30.317  读取 AP boottrace
```

AP boottrace：

```text
primary=26
secondary=10
detail=02150239/00007060/0000000f/00000002/a8000000
```

对应实际事件：

```text
CPU2 进入 secondary vector
  -> CPU2 初始化私有状态、NVIC、Mailbox
  -> CPU2 发送 BOOT_NOTIFY
  -> CPU0 发送 BOOT_PING
  -> CPU2 发送 BOOT_ACK
  -> CPU0 清除 Mailbox pending
  -> CPU0 恢复中断
  -> 第一个中断为 SysTick
  -> SysTick 调用 nxsched_process_timer()
  -> atomic gate 完整释放
  -> nxsched_process_timer() 返回
  -> 后续路径没有到达 stage 27
```

---

**各字段含义**

`detail2=0x0000000f`

```text
IRQ 15 = SysTick
```

所以第一个被 CPU0 接受的中断确实是 SysTick，不是 Mailbox IRQ。

`detail3=0x00000002`

当前 SysTick ISR 的探针逻辑是：

```c
detail[3] = 1;
nxsched_process_timer();
detail[3] = 2;
```

因此这个值证明：

- `nxsched_process_timer()` 已经返回；
- 不只是 `clock_timer()` 返回；
- SMP scheduler tick processing、watchdog timer 路径也已经完成返回；
- 当前停点不再是此前怀疑的首次 atomic/seqlock 操作内部。

`detail4=0xa8000000`

这是：

```text
BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED
```

表示 Peterson atomic gate 至少有一次完成了完整释放：

```text
depth 减到 0
owner 清零
当前 CPU 的 interested 清零
DSB
SEV
```

但它不是当前 PC 位置，只是最后一次 gate 探针状态。它不能单独证明后续没有再次进入锁路径。

---

**当前精确卡点**

当前阶段定义为：

```text
25  CPU2 handshake 完成，准备恢复 CPU0 中断
26  CPU0 第一个中断已经进入 NuttX dispatch
27  up_irq_restore() 返回
28  up_cpu_start() 即将成功返回
30  late bring-up 开始
34  PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY 已发送并确认
```

现在停在：

```text
primary=26
```

因此还没有执行到：

```text
stage 27: up_irq_restore() 调用后的 C 代码
stage 28: up_cpu_start() 返回
stage 30: nx_smp_start()/late bring-up 后续
stage 34: PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD
```

需要注意，`primary=26` 不代表处理器仍然在 `nxsched_process_timer()`。`detail3=2` 已经证明它离开了该函数。

当前未被观测的代码区间是：

```text
bk7258_timerisr() 写入 detail3=2
  -> irq_dispatch() 返回
  -> exception_direct() 检查 running task / assigned task
  -> 可能触发 PendSV
  -> 可能 tail-chain 到 PendSV
  -> 可能执行 arm_doirq() 和上下文恢复
  -> SysTick 异常返回
  -> up_cpu_start() 继续执行
  -> stage 27
```

---

**最可能的原因**

**1. SysTick 返回后触发了 PendSV，卡在 PendSV 或其原子路径**

`exception_direct()` 在 IRQ dispatch 返回后会比较：

```text
g_running_tasks[cpu]
g_assignedtasks[cpu]
```

如果二者不同，就会设置 PendSV：

```text
up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0)
```

这个路径可能进入：

```text
up_trigger_irq()
  -> modifyreg32()
  -> atomic_lock()
  -> BK7258 Peterson gate
```

或者随后 tail-chain 到：

```text
PendSV
  -> exception_common
  -> arm_doirq
  -> nxsched_suspend_scheduler
  -> scheduler/context switch
  -> board_autoled_on/off
  -> context restore
  -> exception return
```

这与当前日志相容：

- timer body 已返回；
- gate 已完整释放；
- 但 `exception_direct()` 后续没有完成；
- stage 27 没有机会执行。

这是目前最值得优先验证的路径。

**2. PendSV 上下文恢复阶段触发 Fault**

如果 SysTick 触发了 PendSV，可能在以下操作中出错：

```text
保存/选择 tcb->xcp.regs
恢复 PSP/MSP
恢复 PSPLIM/MSPLIM
恢复 BASEPRI/CONTROL
执行 EXC_RETURN
```

当前启用了：

```text
CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE=y
CONFIG_ARM_MPU=y
```

因此无效的栈指针、PSPLIM 或异常帧可能在异常返回时触发 MemManage/BusFault/HardFault。此类 fault 发生在 `detail3=2` 之后，也会留下：

```text
primary=26
detail3=2
```

**3. `up_irq_restore()` 之后发生中断重入或中断风暴**

`up_cpu_start()` 的关键汇编顺序是：

```asm
msr BASEPRI, saved_flags
bl  bk7258_boottrace_primary(27)
```

恢复 BASEPRI 后，到写入 stage 27 之间没有显式 `DSB/ISB`。因此任何 pending IRQ 都可以在 stage 27 前抢占。

正常情况下，从 `up_irq_restore()` 到 stage 27 只有几条指令，不应被 1 kHz SysTick 长时间阻塞。但如果存在：

- SysTick 立即重复 pending；
- Mailbox IRQ 持续重新触发；
- PendSV 被持续触发；
- 某个 IRQ handler 没有正确清 pending；

就可能长期看不到 stage 27。

**4. 直接 SysTick 的硬件异常返回失败**

SysTick 使用的是 `exception_direct`，不是完整的 `exception_common`。`detail3=2` 写入后仍然要经过：

```asm
pop {r4, pc}
bx  EXC_RETURN
```

如果硬件异常帧、MSP、MSPLIM 或 EXC_RETURN 有问题，可能在自动 unstack 时触发 fault。这个可能性低于 PendSV，但目前不能排除。

---

**原厂行为与当前实现的核心区别**

| 项目 | 原厂 FreeRTOS SMP | 当前 OpenVela |
|---|---|---|
| AP 主核 | FreeRTOS logical CPU0 | NuttX logical CPU0 |
| AP 次核 | FreeRTOS logical CPU1，对应物理 CPU2 | NuttX logical CPU1，对应物理 CPU2 |
| 次核启动 | `multicore_launch_core1()` | 显式 reset/vector/status 控制 |
| 次核确认 | 主要依赖固定 busy delay | `BOOT_NOTIFY -> BOOT_PING -> BOOT_ACK` |
| 次核中断 | 先初始化，scheduler handoff 期间保持全局中断关闭 | notify 后执行 `up_irq_enable()` |
| 主核 scheduler 启动 | 释放次核后 busy wait，再启动 FreeRTOS scheduler | `nx_start()` 内调用 `nx_smp_start()` |
| 首次任务 | `cpsie i -> SVC -> vRestoreContextOfFirstTask()` | NuttX idle/scheduler 路径 |
| Tick owner | `configTICK_CORE=CPU0_CORE_ID` | NuttX logical CPU0 |
| 次核 SysTick | scheduler startup 中也配置，但非主核走 other-core tick 逻辑 | 当前显式关闭 CPU1 private SysTick |
| CP ready | 原厂 PM/heartbeat 机制较早介入 | 先完成 SMP、worker、link、PWC，再发送 `0x5` |
| 最终 ready | 没有独立 OpenVela ready commit | `0x5` 为 boot ready，`0x11` 为 OpenVela final ready |

最重要的差异是中断恢复时机。

原厂 FreeRTOS 的次核路径在首次任务启动前保持全局中断关闭，并通过：

```text
cpsie i
SVC
恢复第一任务上下文
```

进入正常调度。

当前 OpenVela 在 `up_cpu_start()` 中：

```text
完成 CPU2 ACK
清理 Mailbox pending
恢复 CPU0 BASEPRI
```

这会让一个已经 pending 的 SysTick 在 `up_cpu_start()` 尚未返回前立即进入。也就是说，当前实现把第一个 SysTick 放在了 CPU2 启动函数的中间，而原厂实现没有暴露完全相同的启动窗口。

这不是说当前设计一定错误，但它是当前日志暴露出来的最大时序差异。

---

**CP 超时的准确含义**

```text
CP:E(10113):CPU1 boot timeout stage=4
E(10115):OpenVela AP boot transaction failed: -4102
```

这里的 `stage=4` 是 CP 侧 PM boot transaction stage，不是 AP boottrace 的 `primary=4`。

当前 AP 还没有到：

```text
primary=30  late bring-up
primary=33  PWC start
primary=34  PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY sent
```

所以 CP 没有收到当前实现要求的：

```text
PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD = 0x5
```

CP 的：

```text
IPC retry to start core1, retry_cnt:4
```

更像是 CP 在等待 AP boot transaction 完成期间对 IPC/启动事件的重试，不应直接解释成物理 CPU1 被重新完整复位了四次。当前 boottrace 仍保持 `primary=26`，也支持“AP 一直卡在同一次启动过程”这一判断。

---

**已经可以排除的方向**

当前日志基本排除了：

- CPU2 reset release 失败；
- CPU2 vector 地址错误；
- CPU2 bootstrap stack 错误；
- CPU2 NVIC/private 初始化失败；
- CPU2 mailbox 初始化失败；
- `BOOT_NOTIFY` 没有发送；
- `BOOT_PING` 没有发送；
- `BOOT_ACK` 没有发送；
- CPU0 没有收到 ACK；
- CPU0 没有进入首个中断；
- 首次 SysTick 卡在 `clock_timer()` 的第一次 atomic gate；
- 首次 `nxsched_process_timer()` 未返回；
- 首个 IRQ 是 Mailbox 而非 SysTick；
- 当前 480 MHz/4 divider 的 CP readback 明显异常；
- PSRAM 初始化失败。

日志中的以下信息不是当前卡点的直接证据：

```text
load polar tab magic code error 0xffffffff
```

这是 Wi-Fi RF calibration 数据缺失或未烧录相关表项的校准警告。因为后续 Wi-Fi 已初始化成功，且 AP 已进入 SMP 首中断阶段，它不是当前 `primary=26` 停止的主要原因。

---

**下一步最有价值的验证**

当前不应该继续优先修改 Peterson gate。它已经完成了至少一次完整 acquire/release，且 `detail3=2` 证明 timer processing 已返回。

下一轮应针对 `exception_direct()` 的后半段增加区分性观测，优先记录：

```text
A. detail5: g_running_tasks[0] == g_assignedtasks[0] ?
B. detail6: 是否执行了 up_trigger_irq(PendSV) ?
C. detail7: 进入/离开 exception_direct()
D. fault handler: IPSR、CFSR、HFSR、MMFAR、BFAR、EXC_RETURN、MSP、PSP
```

判断方式：

```text
task pointers 相等
  -> 没有 PendSV 请求
  -> 优先检查 BASEPRI 恢复后的 IRQ 重入/异常返回

task pointers 不等
  -> 进入 PendSV
  -> 优先检查 modifyreg32/atomic gate、arm_doirq、PSP/PSPLIM 和 context restore

触发了 PendSV，但没有离开
  -> 重点检查 exception_common/arm_doirq/LED GPIO/上下文恢复

exception_direct 离开，但 stage27 仍未写
  -> 重点检查异常 tail-chain 或异常返回后的 fault
```

最小化诊断顺序应是：

```text
timer ISR return
  -> exception_direct post-dispatch entry
  -> task mismatch result
  -> PendSV pending request
  -> exception_direct exit
  -> stage 27
```

如果允许下一轮固件修改，优先在 `exception_direct` 的 post-dispatch 分支和 fault handler 加 trace，而不是再扩大 gate 内部探针。 текущ日志已经表明真正需要区分的是：

```text
没有触发 PendSV
还是
触发 PendSV 后卡住
还是
PendSV 返回但自动异常返回失败
还是
中断恢复后发生连续重入
```

目前的软件启动链已经通过 CPU2 硬件启动和 Mailbox handshake；剩余问题集中在“在 `up_cpu_start()` 内恢复中断后，首个 SysTick 与 NuttX 的异常/调度返回路径发生交互”这一段。

现在尝试进行修复。以上述分析为准，下述作为参考意见：当前主嫌（按可能性排序）1. 首次 IPI 到 CPU2 失败 → 静默 PANIC（最吻合 trace） 证据：detail3=2（tick 完成）+ detail4=0xa8000000（门锁干净释放后零活动）→ 挂点正好落在"门锁之后的 gate-free 代码"。唯一能完全对上"最后门锁=RELEASED、之后无任何痕迹"的路径是：up_send_smp_sched(1) → bk7258_smp_kick → cmpxchg（门锁）→ bk7258_mbox_send(CH2) FIFO 满 → 1024 次 nop 重试（无门锁无 trace）→ -ETIMEDOUT → PANIC（bk7258_smpcall.c:169-193）→ syslog 缓冲未转发 = 静默挂死。22:16 已修复 kicked 标志残留，但"首个 kick 超时即 PANIC"仍在。


2. CPU2 在 ACK 后卡死/死亡（导致 FIFO 无人排空） 证据：secondary=10（ACK）后无任何 CPU2 活动记录。CPU2 若卡在 nx_idle_trampoline 前（如 sched_note_cpu_started/栈切换），后续 kick 消息堆满 CH2 FIFO（深度 3）→ 触发主嫌 1 的 FIFO 满。无 liveness 标记，无法排除。


3. IRQ 收尾/上下文切换路径挂死（低-中） tick 返回后 epilogue（arm_switchcontext/nxsched_merge_pending）不碰门锁、无探针，trace 无法覆盖，理论上不能排除。


4. mailbox IRQ 排空循环挂死（低） bk7258_mbox_irq 的 while 排空循环若 FIFO 持续有数据会无限循环。此窗口内 CPU2 已空闲、无消息源，可能性低但未排除（需加出入口 trace 确认）。

100:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
101: }
102: 
103: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
104: {
105:   int cpu = this_cpu();
106: 
107:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)
108:     {
109:       if (cpu == 0)
110:         {
111:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY;
112:         }
113: 
114:       return;
115:     }
116: 
117:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
118:     {
119:       if (cpu == 1 &&
120:           bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK) < 0)
121:         {
122:           PANIC();
123:         }
124: 
125:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK);
126:       return;
127:     }
128: 
129:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK)
130:     {
131:       if (cpu == 0)
132:         {
133:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK;
134:         }
135: 
136:       return;
137:     }
138: 
139:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
140:     {
141:       return;
142:     }
143: 
144:   for (;;)
145:     {
146:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
147: 
148:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
149:         {
150:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
151:         }
152: 
153:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
154:         {
155:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
156:         }
157: 
158:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
159:       UP_DMB();
160:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
161:         {
162:           break;
163:         }
164: 
165:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
166:     }
167: }
168: 
169: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
170: {
171:   int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
172: 
173:   if (ret < 0)
174:     {
175:       PANIC();
176:     }
177: 
178:   return ret;
179: }
180: 
181: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
182: {
183:   int cpu;
184: 
185:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1u << cpu))
186:     {
187:       cpu = ffs((int)cpuset) - 1;
188:       if (cpu != this_cpu() && bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_CALL) < 0)
189:         {
190:           PANIC();
191:         }
192:     }
193: }
194: 
195: void bk7258_smp_prepare_boot(void)
196: {
197:   int cpu;
198: 
199:   for (cpu = 0; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
200:     {
201:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
202:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
203:     }
204: 
205:   g_boot_seen = 0;
206:   UP_DMB();
207: }
208: 
209: void bk7258_smp_boot_notify(void)
210: {
211:   if (bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY) < 0)
212:     {
213:       PANIC();
214:     }
215: }

217: bool bk7258_smp_boot_notified(void)
218: {
219:   return (g_boot_seen & BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY) != 0;
220: }

222: bool bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete(void)
223: {
224:   return g_boot_seen == (BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY |
225:                          BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK);
226: }

230:   return bk7258_smp_boot_send(cpu, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING);

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 CPU2 startup.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>

10: #include <stdint.h>
11: #include <syslog.h>
12: 
13: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
14: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>

16: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
17: #include <nuttx/sched_note.h>
18: 
19: #include "arm_internal.h"
20: #include "dwt.h"
21: #include "init/init.h"
22: #include "nvic.h"
23: #include "sched/sched.h"

25: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
26: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
27: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
28: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
29: 
30: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS != 2
31: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP supports exactly two AP CPUs"
32: #endif
33: 
34: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ != 480000000
35: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP requires the fixed 480 MHz CP contract"
36: #endif
37: 
38: #define BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES  (CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / 2u)
39: #define BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT     4000000u
40: 
41: extern uint8_t __secondary_vectors_start[];
42: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_base[];
43: 
44: static void bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset(void)
45: {
46:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
47:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
48:   UP_DSB();
49: }
50: 
51: static void bk7258_cpu2_release_reset(void)
52: {
53:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
54:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
55:   UP_DSB();
56:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
57: }
58: 
59: static void __attribute__((used, noreturn)) bk7258_secondary_idle(void)
60: {
61:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
62:   arm_initialize_stack();
63:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_STACK);
64:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);
65:   bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
66:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
67:   up_irq_enable();
68:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ_ON);
69:   sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
70:   nx_idle_trampoline();
71:   PANIC();
72: }
73: 
74: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
75: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
76:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
77: {
78:   __asm__ volatile
79:     (
80:       "msr psp, r0\n"
81: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
82:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
83: #endif
84:       "mrs r1, control\n"
85:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
86:       "msr control, r1\n"
87:       "isb sy\n"
88:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
89:     );
90: }
91: 
92: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
93:                            target("general-regs-only")))
94: bk7258_secondary_boot(void)
95: {
96:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
97:   uintptr_t idle_top;
98: 
99:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ENTRY);
100:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
101:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
102:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
104:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
105:     {
106:       PANIC();
107:     }
108: 
109:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
110: 
111:   tcb = current_task(1);
112:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
113:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);
114: }
115: 
116: void __attribute__((naked, noreturn, section(".start_text")))
117: bk7258_secondary_start(void)
118: {
119:   __asm__ volatile
120:     (
121:       "cpsid i\n"
122:       "movs r0, #1\n"
123:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
124:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
125:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
126:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
127:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
128:     );
129: }
130: 
131: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
132: {
133:   irqstate_t flags;
134:   uint32_t started;
135:   uint32_t polls = 0;
136:   uint32_t control;
137:   uint32_t status;
138:   bool ping_sent = false;
139: 
140:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
141: 
142:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
143:     {
144:       return -EINVAL;
145:     }
146: 
147:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
148:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
149:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
150:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
151:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
152:     {
153:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
154:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
155:       PANIC();
156:     }
157: 
158:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
159:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
160:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
161:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
162:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
163:     {
164:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
165:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
166:       PANIC();
167:     }
168: 
169:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
170:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
171:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
172: 
173:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
174:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
175:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
176:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
177:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
178:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
179:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
180:   UP_DMB();
181:   UP_DSB();
182: 
183:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
184:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
185:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
186:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
187:   flags = up_irq_save();
188:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
189:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
190:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
191:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
192: 
193:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
194:     {
195:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
196:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
197:         {
198:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
199:             {
200:               break;
201:             }
202: 
203:           ping_sent = true;
204:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
205:         }
206: 
207:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
208:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
209:         {
210:           break;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
215:     {
216:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
217:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
218:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
219:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
220:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
221:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
222:       up_irq_restore(flags);
223:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
224:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
225:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
226:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
227:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
228:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
229:       PANIC();
230:     }
231: 
232:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
233:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
234:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
235:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
236:   UP_DSB();
237:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
238:   up_irq_restore(flags);
239:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
240:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
241:   return OK;
242: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 MBOX0 v2 physical transport.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <string.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
14: 
15: #include "arm_internal.h"
16: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
17: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
18: #include "irq.h"
19: 
20: #define MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT      (2u * 3u + 1u)
21: 
22: struct mbox_rx_descriptor
23: {
24:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
25:   uint32_t order;
26:   bool used;
27: };
28: 
29: static bk7258_mbox_callback_t g_callback;
30: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor g_rx_desc[MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT];
31: static uint32_t g_rx_order;
32: static uint32_t g_processing_order;
33: static bool g_mbox_ready;
34: static bool g_mbox_smp_ready;
35: static struct bk7258_mbox_stats g_stats;
36: 
37: _Static_assert(MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT > 2u * 3u,
38:                "RX descriptors must hold a deferred command and two FIFOs");
39: 
40: uint32_t bk7258_mbox_rx_status(void)
41: {
42:   return getreg32(up_cpu_index() == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
43:                                        BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS);
44: }
45: 
46: static void mbox_clear_errors(int cpu)
47: {
48:   uintptr_t cfg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG;
49:   uint32_t config = getreg32(cfg);
50:   uint32_t errors = config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS;
51: 
52:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS) != 0)
53:     {
54:       g_stats.write_error++;
55:     }
56: 
57:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS) != 0)
58:     {
59:       g_stats.read_error++;
60:     }
61: 
62:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS) != 0)
63:     {
64:       g_stats.write_full++;
65:     }
66: 
67:   if (errors != 0)
68:     {
69:       putreg32((config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, cfg);
70:     }
71: }
72: 
73: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
74:                                 uint32_t length)
75: {
76:   if (source != 0)
77:     {
78:       g_stats.bad_source++;
79:       return false;
80:     }
81: 
82:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
83:     {
84:       g_stats.bad_length++;
85:       return false;
86:     }
87: 
88:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
89:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
90:     {
91:       g_stats.bad_address++;
92:       return false;
93:     }
94: 
95:   return true;
96: }
97: 
98: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
99: {
100:   uintptr_t status;
101:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
102: 
103:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
104:     {
105:       return -EINVAL;
106:     }
107: 
108: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
109:   if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
110:     {
111:       return -EPERM;
112:     }
113: #endif
114: 
115:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
116:    * receive FIFO status register.
117:    */
118: 
119:   status = destination == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
120:             destination == 1 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
121:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
122:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
123:     {
124:       return -EAGAIN;
125:     }
126: 
127:   putreg32(data[0], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA0 :
128:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA0);
129:   putreg32(data[1], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA1 :
130:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA1);
131:   putreg32(destination, cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TID :
132:                                   BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TID);
133:   return OK;
134: }
135: 
136: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
137: {
138:   unsigned int i;
139: 
140:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
141:     {
142:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)
143:         {
144:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
145:         }
146:     }
147: 
148:   return NULL;
149: }
150: 
151: static bool mbox_priority_message(
152:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
153: {
154:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
155: 
156:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
157: }
158: 
159: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
160: {
161:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
162:   unsigned int i;
163: 
164:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
165:     {
166:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
167: 
168:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
169:         {
170:           continue;
171:         }
172: 
173:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
174:         {
175:           oldest = desc;
176:         }
177:     }
178: 
179:   return oldest;
180: }
181: 
182: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
183: {
184:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
185:   int ret;
186: 
187:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
188:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
189:    */
190: 
191:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
192:     {
193:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
194:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
195:       g_processing_order = 0;
196:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
197:         {
198:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
199:           break;
200:         }
201: 
202:       desc->used = false;
203:     }
204: 
205:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
206:     {
207:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
208:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
209:       g_processing_order = 0;
210:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
211:         {
212:           break;
213:         }
214: 
215:       desc->used = false;
216:     }
217: }
218: 
219: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
220: {
221:   uintptr_t rdata0;
222:   uintptr_t rdata1;
223:   uintptr_t sidreg;
224:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
225: 
226:   (void)irq;
227:   (void)context;
228:   (void)arg;
229: 
230:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
231:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;

52:  *
53:  * Description:
54:  *   This is the common start-up logic for the IDLE task for CPUs 1 through
55:  *   (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).  Having a start-up function such as this for the
56:  *   IDLE is not really an architectural necessity.  It is used only for
57:  *   symmetry with how other threads are started (see nxtask_start() and
58:  *   pthread_start()).
59:  *
60:  * Input Parameters:
61:  *   None.
62:  *
63:  * Returned Value:
64:  *   This function does not return.
65:  *
66:  ****************************************************************************/

68: void nx_idle_trampoline(void)
69: {
70: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_SWITCH
71:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = this_task();
72: 
73:   /* Announce that the IDLE task has started */
74: 
75:   sched_note_start(tcb);
76: #endif
77: 
78:   /* wait until cpu0 in idle() */
79: 
80:   while (!OSINIT_IDLELOOP());
81: 
82:   sched_unlock();
83: 
84:   /* Enter the IDLE loop */
85: 
86:   sinfo("CPU%d: Beginning Idle Loop\n", this_cpu());
87: 
88:   for (; ; )

97:  * Name: nx_smp_start
98:  *
99:  * Description:
100:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
101:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion
102:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
103:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
104:  *   function.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   None
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
111:  *
112:  * Assumption:
113:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
114:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
115:  *
116:  ****************************************************************************/
117: 
118: int nx_smp_start(void)
119: {
120:   int ret;
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
124: 
125:   up_flush_dcache_all();
126: 
127:   /* Start all of the other CPUs.  CPU0 is already running. */
128: 
129:   for (cpu = 1; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)

132:

137:           return ret;
138:         }
139:     }

+detail[4]=b1xxxxxx: CPU0 进入 raw kick
+detail[4]=b2xxxxxx: kick 已被现有 g_ipi_kicked 合并
+detail[4]=b3xxxxxx: FIFO 写入成功

已按当前主嫌完成修复，并生成新的可烧录固件。

**修复内容**

1. **移除首个 scheduler IPI 失败后的立即 `PANIC()`**
   - `up_send_smp_sched()` 不再因 `CH2 FIFO` 暂时满而直接死机。
   - `up_send_smp_call()` 同样不再因 IPI 发送失败直接 `PANIC()`。
   - `g_ipi_pending` 保留未处理位。
   - 发送失败时清除 `g_ipi_kicked`，允许后续重新发送合并后的 raw kick。
   - CPU0 的后续 SysTick 会调用 `bk7258_smp_retry_pending()` 继续重试。

相关文件：

- `board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c`
- `board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_smp.h`

2. **推迟 SysTick 启动**
   - `up_timer_initialize()` 现在只完成：
     - SysTick priority 配置
     - reload 配置
     - ISR attach
   - 不再在 `clock_initialize()` 阶段立即 enable SysTick。
   - SysTick 改为在 `board_late_initialize()` 进入 bring-up 时启动。
   - 这样避免首个 SysTick 在 `up_cpu_start()` 的：
     ```text
     up_irq_restore()
       -> exception_direct()
       -> PendSV/异常返回
     ```
     窗口中抢占。

相关文件：

- `board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c`
- `board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c`

新增启动阶段：

primary=29

表示 SysTick 已正式启动。

```text
11  sched_note_cpu_started() 已完成
12  已进入 nx_idle_trampoline，等待 CPU0 进入 idle loop

- `bk7258_boottrace.h`

```text
14  Mailbox IRQ 入口

```

同时将单次 Mailbox IRQ 的 FIFO 排空限制为最多 8 个 entry，避免 FIFO 持续有数据时无限循环占用 CPU。

相关文件：

- `bk7258_mbox0.c`
- `bk7258_boottrace.h`

```text
0xb1xxxxxx  进入 kick

0xb4xxxxxx  发送失败，低 16 位为 errno

The most likely sequence is:

2. AP sends RESET followed by a UART0 STATE probe.
3. CP hardware IRQ receives and copies the envelope into its software RX descriptor pool.
4. CP does not dispatch that descriptor because upper-layer mailbox processing occurs only from the lower-priority `ap_console` task.
5. The CP PM boot path enters a non-yielding 10-second AON-RTC busy loop.

The AP TX worker checks active transaction age every 10 ms. A probe expires after 200 ms and moves the link to DOWN; DOWN retries after 100 ms: [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:871) through [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:906](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:906).

PROBING: STATE sent
200 ms: probe timeout
DOWN
100 ms: new recovery epoch
ABORTING: RESET pending
...
```

   The 200 ms timestamp is assigned only after `send_slot()` succeeds: [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:524). **CP protocol comparison**

The CP implementation has the same logical protocol fields:

- UART DATA command: command 0, pointer, length, RTS.
- UART STATE command: command 1, null pointer, zero length, RTS.
- ACK carries RTS and TX-fail in the first ACK data word.
- RESET is an ACK-box control message.

A failed transaction clears the link and schedules recovery: [mb_uart_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_uart_driver.c:408) through [mb_uart_driver.c:497](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_uart_driver.c:497).

The CP physical layer also has a 200 ms timeout, but it is checked only from `mb_chnl_poll()`: [mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:1147) through [mailbox_channel.c:1195](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mailbox_channel.c:1195). Consequently, the same CP poll starvation prevents CP-side physical timeout and RESET recovery as well as UART ACK generation.
